narrativeReportMd:
# ProdCharacteristic R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ProdCharacteristic` is present in R4 but absent from the R6 ballot core package as a standalone datatype. This is a high-impact breaking identity and code-generation change: validators, generated models, profiles, and transforms that reference the R4 canonical datatype cannot resolve the same artifact in R6.

## Scope
The assessment covers the local R4 `ProdCharacteristic` StructureDefinition and the absence of a same-named R6 StructureDefinition. I also inspected likely R6 successor surfaces in product/package/device resources only to characterize migration risk; full resource-level migration belongs to those resource reports.

## Main migration themes
R4 used named fields such as `height`, `width`, `shape`, `color`, `imprint`, `image`, and `scoring`. R6 appears to model similar information through repeating coded property/characteristic components with a required `type` and a choice `value[x]`. That is not a path-preserving rename: migration needs explicit semantic mapping from each old field name to a code, plus value-type decisions for string appearance fields.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issue is the removal of the datatype identity itself. The second major issue is the loss of the strongly named local content model, which affects JSON/XML paths, FHIRPath expressions, generated classes, and validation profiles. A separate R6-to-R4 risk exists because the likely R6 successor property models allow value kinds that do not fit the old `ProdCharacteristic` field set.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most needed for the exact successor mapping. The local computable definitions show the absence and the candidate R6 patterns, but no supplied official diff, ConceptMap, or terminology expansion proves a complete one-to-one migration.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive design could have kept `ProdCharacteristic` as a deprecated compatibility datatype or published an explicit cross-version extension/ConceptMap. The tradeoff would have been carrying legacy paths while R6 moved toward more generic, context-specific characteristic modeling.

## Follow-up analysis
The containing resource reports should own detailed migration of R4 `DeviceDefinition.physicalCharacteristics`, `MedicinalProductManufactured.physicalCharacteristics`, and `MedicinalProductPackaged.packageItem.physicalCharacteristics` to their R6 resource-specific structures.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ProdCharacteristic` has no same-canonical R6 datatype, so this is a confirmed breaking identity change. The top concerns are unresolved canonical/type references, conversion from named fields to coded property structures, and lossy reverse mapping from broader R6 property values. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official R4-to-R6 ConceptMap or ballot rationale.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should not treat this as a simple rename. R4 paths such as `ProdCharacteristic.height` and `ProdCharacteristic.color` need to become context-specific R6 property entries with a characteristic `type` code and an appropriate `value[x]`. Existing generated code that exposes a `ProdCharacteristic` class or FHIRPath expressions over named fields must be replaced with resource-specific property traversal. R6-to-R4 conversion will be lossy unless the R6 property type code is recognized and the value type fits one of the old named fields.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the datatype is absent: the expected file is missing and the R6 package index has no matching StructureDefinition id, URL, or filename. Confidence is medium for exact successor mapping because the R6 package contains several plausible resource-specific property/characteristic structures, but the supplied inputs do not include an official diff, migration guide, or ConceptMap proving the intended mapping for every field.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 artifact exists at canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/ProdCharacteristic`, kind `complex-type`, type `ProdCharacteristic`, derivation `specialization`, base `BackboneElement`, and `abstract=false`.

newState.summary: No same-id, same-canonical R6 StructureDefinition exists in the supplied core package.
newState.narrativeMd: The expected R6 file `StructureDefinition-ProdCharacteristic.json` is absent, and the R6 package index has no matching `StructureDefinition` entry. The nearest R6 patterns are embedded resource-specific `property` or `characteristic` BackboneElements rather than a reusable datatype.

facts.note: No R6 StructureDefinition id with this value was found.
No R6 StructureDefinition with this canonical URL was found.
The expected R6 file is absent.
Observed in DeviceDefinition, MedicinalProductDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, ManufacturedItemDefinition, and AdministrableProductDefinition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old artifact was matched by exact id, canonical URL, type, and filename. No exact R6 match exists. Candidate R6 elements were identified by product/device characteristic semantics, but they are not the same artifact identity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct artifact-resolution break. R4 profiles, generated classes, serializers, validators, and FHIRPath expressions that refer to the `ProdCharacteristic` canonical or type cannot resolve the same datatype in R6. Embedded R4 content using this datatype is not R6-valid by retaining the same datatype identity.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The affected data describes product, packaging, manufactured item, and device characteristics. Loss or mis-mapping can affect regulatory submissions, product identification, package/device matching, and user-facing product descriptions, though the datatype itself is not generally a direct clinical observation.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace a reusable R4 physical-characteristics datatype with context-specific characteristic/property modeling in R6 resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `ProdCharacteristic` as a deprecated R6 compatibility datatype while introducing the resource-specific property/characteristic model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of moving product and device characteristics into context-specific coded property structures is reasonable, but the hard removal of the `ProdCharacteristic` canonical/type identity was probably avoidable. A deprecated compatibility StructureDefinition could have allowed old canonical references, generated classes, profile differentials, and validators to resolve while R6 resources used the newer model. The supplied evidence does not show why that compatibility artifact would have prevented the R6 redesign.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would retain `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/ProdCharacteristic` in R6 with the old shape, clearly mark it deprecated/legacy, and point implementers to the new resource-specific `property` or `characteristic` structures for new work. That is more than migration guidance because the base R6 package would still contain the old artifact. The tradeoff is a larger legacy surface and a risk that some implementations keep depending on the retired datatype, but this tradeoff is moderate for the artifact-identity issue and does not by itself require duplicate same-resource fields.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves canonical and generated-type compatibility at the cost of carrying a legacy artifact that R6 no longer wants implementers to prefer.

evidence.detail: The expected R6 StructureDefinition file is absent.
The R6 package index has no matching StructureDefinition entry for ProdCharacteristic.

examples.examplesMd: The example is an illustrative R4 datatype fragment, not a complete resource. In R6 there is no `ProdCharacteristic` datatype against which this same fragment can validate.

findings.narrativeMd: `ProdCharacteristic` was removed as a standalone datatype identity in the supplied R6 core package. That matters even before field-level mapping because many implementation artifacts key on canonical URL or generated type name. A validator cannot resolve the old canonical in R6, and generated code will not expose the same class unless a vendor keeps a non-standard compatibility model.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance fragment valid as a `ProdCharacteristic` cannot be made R6-valid by simply changing the package version, because the R6 core package has no corresponding StructureDefinition. The break affects R4-to-R6 validation, profile derivation, StructureDefinition differential references, serializers, schema generation, and type-name based runtime dispatch.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all profiles, transforms, and generated classes that mention `ProdCharacteristic` or its canonical URL. Replace references with context-specific R6 resource paths and define an explicit mapping for each old field. Tests should include resolution of canonical URLs, generated model compilation, validation of migrated examples, and failure cases for unmapped characteristics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal could have been softened by retaining the R4 datatype as deprecated or by publishing an official compatibility extension/ConceptMap. That would preserve old references while allowing R6 resources to prefer generic property structures. Without such a bridge, implementers must create local mappings and accept non-portable behavior until a standard map is available.

findings.title: Named ProdCharacteristic fields are not path-preserved in likely R6 successor models

oldState.summary: R4 has named local fields for dimensions, appearance, images, and scoring.

semanticText.definition: R4 defines optional local fields: six 0..1 Quantity fields for dimensions or weight/volume/diameter, `shape` 0..1 string, `color` and `imprint` 0..* string, `image` 0..* Attachment, and `scoring` 0..1 CodeableConcept.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 datatype encodes the characteristic kind in the element name. For example, `height` is a `Quantity`, `color` is a repeating `string`, and `image` is a repeating `Attachment`.

newState.summary: R6 does not retain these fields as datatype paths; similar data appears to require generic coded property entries.

semanticText.definition: Candidate R6 successors use repeating BackboneElements with a mandatory `type` CodeableConcept and a choice `value[x]`, such as `ManufacturedItemDefinition.property.type` and `ManufacturedItemDefinition.property.value[x]`.

newState.narrativeMd: The likely R6 shape is a list of coded properties, not a reusable datatype with fixed field names. Migrating `height` or `color` therefore requires adding a `type` coding that says which characteristic is represented.

facts.note: These local element paths have no same-path R6 datatype counterpart.
Seen in R6 resource-specific property/characteristic components.
Candidate R6 property/characteristic components require the characteristic type code.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The semantic overlap is strong for product and device characteristics, but the match is not an exact artifact rename. It is a structural remodeling from named fields to coded generic properties.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 JSON/XML paths such as `height`, `color`, or `image` are not accepted by an R6 model that lacks the datatype. Even where the same concept can be expressed, it must be transformed into repeated property entries and augmented with a characteristic type code. This is high risk for generated classes, FHIRPath queries, profile differentials, and hand-written serializers.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect mapping of dimensions, package appearance, imprints, or images can cause product identification and regulatory data quality issues.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize many physical and descriptive characteristics into extensible coded property lists.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the old named fields as deprecated aliases or a compatibility datatype while adding generic coded property entries.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is stronger here than simple deletion: R6 appears to replace a fixed list of named fields with extensible coded `type` plus `value[x]` property components. That goal is reasonable for product, package, manufactured item, administrable product, and device characteristics. A less-breaking alias period was possible, but it would have duplicated the same facts as both old named slots and new coded entries across multiple resource contexts, creating validation ambiguity and interoperability burden. Given those material tradeoffs, the break is probably justified, though the absence of an authoritative field-to-code map remains a migration weakness.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial alternative would keep fields such as `height`, `color`, `imprint`, `image`, and `scoring` as deprecated compatibility paths while adding the new coded property list. Invariants or conversion rules could discourage simultaneous conflicting use, and a standard map from field names to `property.type` codes would make conversion safer. This would preserve many R4-valid patterns but would not be clean long term: the same characteristic could appear in two places, old fields might never disappear, and receivers would need to reconcile conflicts.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Aliases would preserve common R4 paths but create duplicate representations for the same characteristic, requiring conflict rules and risking indefinite legacy accumulation.

evidence.detail: A likely R6 successor pattern requires a characteristic type CodeableConcept.
A package-property value is represented as a choice rather than by fixed field names.
DeviceDefinition uses a similar property type/value pattern for fixed characteristics.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is schematic. It shows the likely R6 coded-property shape, but the actual `type` coding system and target resource path require project or standards guidance.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 implementers could treat the datatype as a fixed object with named properties. R6 candidate models instead encode the kind of property in data, usually a `CodeableConcept`, with the value carried in `value[x]`. This is a representation break rather than a harmless rename: existing field accessors, JSON paths, database columns, and profile constraints over `ProdCharacteristic.color` or `ProdCharacteristic.height` will not continue to work.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A same-shape R4 fragment using `height`, `color`, or `imprint` is invalid against R6 because there is no datatype or same-path element to receive those names. Conversely, a converted R6 property entry may be representable in R4 only if its `type` can be recognized as one of the old named fields and its `value[x]` can be reduced to the corresponding old datatype and cardinality.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit mapping table from each R4 field to the target R6 resource path, `type` coding, and `value[x]` type. Treat R4 repeating `color`, `imprint`, and `image` as repeated R6 property entries unless the target resource has a more specific pattern. Validate converted data with examples that include multiple colors, multiple imprints, all Quantity dimensions, image attachments, and unmapped local extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 generic property design could support more characteristic kinds without adding new elements, which is a legitimate modeling goal. However, it could have been introduced less disruptively by keeping named fields as deprecated aliases or by making a standard conversion map part of the release. Without that, implementations must infer or locally govern the mapping.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The finding treats the property/characteristic elements as likely successors based on local R6 StructureDefinitions. Official R6 narrative or cross-version maps could refine which target resource and coding should be used for each old field.

findings.title: Likely R6 successor properties admit values that are not cleanly representable in R4 ProdCharacteristic

oldState.summary: R4 ProdCharacteristic supports a fixed, narrow set of named value slots.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can carry dimensions as `Quantity`, appearance text as `string`, images as `Attachment`, and scoring as `CodeableConcept`. It has no generic coded property type or open `value[x]` slot.

newState.summary: Candidate R6 property models allow broader value types and additional semantics.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 candidate value choices vary by resource. Medicinal/manufactured/administrable product properties include values such as `Range`, `date`, `boolean`, `markdown`, and Binary references; DeviceDefinition.property also includes `integer` and `string`.

facts.note: These do not have direct named slots in R4 ProdCharacteristic.
R4 encodes the characteristic type by field name rather than by a separate coded element.
No status field exists on R4 ProdCharacteristic.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The risk is assessed against plausible successor property models because there is no direct R6 `ProdCharacteristic` artifact.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is primarily a reverse-conversion and round-trip risk. R6 data using a property type not mapped to one of the old named fields, or a value kind such as `Range`, `date`, `boolean`, `markdown`, Binary reference, or `integer`, cannot be represented faithfully in R4 `ProdCharacteristic` without extensions, lossy text conversion, or rejection.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lossy reverse conversion can remove regulatory product qualifiers or product-characteristic status information. The business risk depends on which R6 property types a jurisdiction actually uses.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow R6 resources to express a broader and more flexible set of coded product, package, manufactured item, administrable product, and device characteristics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: This is mainly an R6-to-R4 down-conversion and round-trip limitation, not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The finding describes valid R6 successor property values, such as `Range`, `date`, `boolean`, `markdown`, Binary reference, or status information, that cannot be represented cleanly in the old R4 datatype. That is a real interoperability and round-trip concern, but it is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 base break. Broadening the R6 property value domain is probably justified if the R6 goal is to support more flexible characteristic modeling.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base R6 alternative applies in the calibrated sense because this finding is about reverse conversion from more expressive R6 content to R4. A compatibility profile limiting exchange to R4-compatible property types, standard extensions for non-R4 values, or conversion tooling would help systems that need round-tripping, but those are interoperability mitigations rather than less-breaking base R6 designs. Making the base R6 model only accept the R4-compatible subset would defeat the expanded-value goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Compatibility profiles or extensions can mitigate reverse conversion, but constraining the base R6 property model to the R4 subset would sacrifice the intended R6 expressivity.

evidence.detail: R4 local value-bearing elements are limited to Quantity, string, Attachment, and CodeableConcept fields.
A candidate R6 product-property model allows CodeableConcept, Quantity, Range, date, boolean, markdown, Attachment, and Reference(Binary).
A candidate R6 property model has a status CodeableConcept not present on R4 ProdCharacteristic.
evidence.quote: The status of characteristic e.g. assigned or pending

evidence.detail: DeviceDefinition.property allows value types including integer and string in addition to Quantity, CodeableConcept, boolean, Range, and Attachment.

property.valueMarkdown: Modified release behavior described in markdown.

examples.examplesMd: The example is schematic and uses candidate R6 property shape. R4 `ProdCharacteristic` has no generic `property.type`, no `valueMarkdown`, no `valueBoolean`, and no Binary reference value slot.

findings.narrativeMd: The likely R6 successor property models are more expressive than R4 `ProdCharacteristic`. That helps R6 represent diverse characteristics but creates reverse-mapping risk: a valid R6 property may have no old field name or compatible value type. The issue is especially important for systems that promise bidirectional R4/R6 conversion or store a shared canonical characteristic model internally.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This does not make old R4 content invalid beyond the datatype removal already reported. Instead, it means valid R6 successor content can be impossible to encode in the old R4 datatype without using extensions or lossy conversions. Strict R4 validators would reject invented fields, and generated R4 models have no place for the added value types.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 conversion, define policy per property type: exact map to an old field, map to extension, convert to text with loss marker, or reject. Round-trip tests should include all candidate R6 `value[x]` types, unknown `type` codes, multiple repeated properties of the same type, and administrable-product property status.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The wider R6 property domain is likely useful and partly unavoidable if R6 needed more flexible product characteristics. The backward-compatible alternative is not to prohibit those values globally, but to publish a compatibility profile or cross-version extension strategy for systems that must interoperate with R4.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because there is no direct R6 artifact, this finding is based on likely successor structures. Official cross-version guidance could downgrade or refine the risk for particular resource contexts.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R4 `ProdCharacteristic` local elements have no terminology bindings in the StructureDefinition. Binding changes therefore did not create a separate local finding; coding risk arises from likely R6 successor `type` CodeableConcepts and is covered under conversion findings.

R4 local elements only carry generic inherited constraints such as `ele-1` and extension constraints on `extension`/`modifierExtension`. No ProdCharacteristic-specific invariant was found. Since the R6 datatype is absent, there is no same-artifact R6 constraint set to compare; inherited/base constraints are out of scope.

R4 `ProdCharacteristic` has no local Reference-typed elements. Reference target changes within candidate R6 properties, such as Binary references, are treated as R6-to-R4 conversion risk rather than a direct old-target removal.
No R4 `ProdCharacteristic` local element has a fixed value, pattern value, or default value that could be separately tightened or loosened.
No R4 local element defines maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex constraints beyond its datatype.
No slicing is defined on R4 `ProdCharacteristic` local elements.

No R4 business data element such as `height`, `color`, or `scoring` is marked as a modifier. The only modifier element is inherited `modifierExtension`, which is excluded by the base-artifact scope rule.

The R4 root short/definition text appears to describe marketing status rather than physical characteristics, while the child elements describe dimensions and appearance. Because there is no R6 same-artifact text to compare, this was not raised as a separate semantic-text finding.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R4 `DeviceDefinition.physicalCharacteristics` used `ProdCharacteristic`; R6 `DeviceDefinition.property` appears to be a likely context-specific successor and should be assessed in the DeviceDefinition report.

R4 `MedicinalProductManufactured.physicalCharacteristics` used `ProdCharacteristic`; R6 manufactured item characteristic modeling appears under `ManufacturedItemDefinition.property` and should be assessed by that resource report.

R4 `MedicinalProductPackaged.packageItem.physicalCharacteristics` used `ProdCharacteristic`; R6 package characteristic modeling appears under `PackagedProductDefinition.packaging.property` and needs resource-level analysis.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: A standard mapping from R4 field names such as `height`, `shape`, `color`, and `scoring` to R6 property/characteristic type codes would materially improve migration reliability.

analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use the official HL7 cross-version diff, ballot reconciliation notes, or migration guide for product/device characteristic modeling.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No ConceptMap or authoritative mapping table was available from R4 named fields to R6 property/characteristic type codings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology expansions for the characteristic/property `type` codings used by R6 implementations were not compared. analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare the relevant R6 ValueSets/CodeSystems and any implementation-guide bindings used for product, package, manufactured item, administrable product, and device property types.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative specification pages and examples were not exhaustively reviewed, so the semantic intent of each candidate successor path may be incomplete.
